problem: The lead says the loop exists because a three-way catalyst needs λ held within one percent of 1, then says "Every modern petrol and diesel engine uses this loop". A diesel always runs lean (λ well above 1), has no stoichiometric three-way catalyst, and controls fuel quantity directly; it uses an ECU but not this λ = 1 feedback loop. A student will conclude diesels hold λ = 1.
fix: End the lead with: "Petrol engines use this stoichiometric loop. Diesel engines also have an ECU, but they always run lean (λ well above 1) and control injected fuel quantity directly, cleaning the exhaust with an oxidation catalyst, a particulate filter and selective catalytic reduction instead of a three-way catalyst."

problem: λ is used throughout but never defined as a ratio; "λ = 1, the stoichiometric air-fuel ratio" reads as if λ is itself the air-fuel ratio. Students then cannot say what λ = 1.05 means.
fix: Define it once: "λ (the excess-air ratio) = actual air-fuel ratio ÷ stoichiometric air-fuel ratio. λ = 1 means the mixture is exactly stoichiometric; λ = 1.05 means 5 percent more air than stoichiometric."

problem: The switching oxygen sensor is described only as switching "sharply from lean to rich". The actual voltage values (about 0.1 V lean, about 0.8 to 0.9 V rich for a zirconia sensor) are what the ECU compares against its threshold, and their absence leaves the description incomplete.
fix: Add: "A zirconia switching sensor gives about 0.1 V when the exhaust is lean and about 0.8 to 0.9 V when rich, crossing over within a very small change of λ around 1; the ECU treats roughly 0.45 V as the switch point."

problem: "keeps adaptive trims in electrically erasable memory that survives battery disconnection" is not true of all ECUs; many store learned trims in keep-alive RAM that is lost when the battery is disconnected, which is why the vehicle then relearns its mixture.
fix: Say: "keeps adaptive trims in non-volatile memory (EEPROM or flash) in most modern ECUs; older designs hold them in keep-alive RAM, which loses the learned trims when the battery is disconnected."
